subject: CloudChain: subprocessor certification + KMS attestation
messages:
From: CloudChain Security <security@cloudchain.com>
To: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-06-20T14:03:00Z
Subject: Request: subprocessor roster + SIG/CAIQ/SOC references

Hi Priyom,

Hope you're well — I'm launching the vendor review for our inference stack and need the following for CloudChain's inaugural risk assessment: an up-to-date subprocessor roster (name, location, function, residency), copies of your most recent SOC 2 report (redacted is fine), and any partially completed SIG/CAIQ you can share. We have a few focused questions about KMS ownership for downstream partners (particularly KeyVaultOps and LogStream) and whether any subprocessors have access to plaintext customer content.

Can you confirm ETA for a package (roster + SOC + SIG answers)? Our security review needs an initial bundle by EOD Wednesday PT. If you have an internal contact for KMS flow questions, please loop them in.

Thanks,
Aisha Raman
CloudChain, Vendor Security
security@cloudchain.com

--
Attachment: (none)

From: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
To: CloudChain Security <security@cloudchain.com>, CloudChain Procurement <procurement@cloudchain.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-06-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor roster + SIG/CAIQ/SOC references

Hi Aisha / team,

Thanks for the heads up — we can get you a full package. Attached are: (1) subprocessor_roster_20270621.csv (roster + country + role), (2) SOC2_Type2_Redacted_2026.pdf (latest report, redactions for customer names), and (3) SIG_partial_responses_20270621.xlsx (our responses to most SIG questions; a few technology-specific items are flagged for security).

Quick highlights that may answer your immediate KMS questions:
- We do not store customer plaintext on Redwood systems by default; customer data is processed in-memory during inference and evicted from ephemeral caches per customer-configured retention settings.
- Key management for hosted customers is via our KMS integration: for customers who provide their own KMS, keys never leave the customer's control. For platform-managed keys, we use a segregated KMS tenant with strict RBAC; only our crypto service has the ability to call decrypt in a single limited service boundary.
- KeyVaultOps is a third-party logging/telemetry vendor (logs only); they do not hold decryption keys or have access to plaintext.

Neha (Security) and Lauren (Legal) are copied — they'll follow up on the flagged SIG items and provide a short attestation note about subprocessor access if needed.

ETA: initial bundle (attached) delivered now; Neha will send a KMS flow diagram and an attestation email by EOD Thursday PT.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Partner Ops, Redwood Inference
pri yom.das@redwoodinference.com

--
Attachments: subprocessor_roster_20270621.csv; SOC2_Type2_Redacted_2026.pdf; SIG_partial_responses_20270621.xlsx

From: CloudChain Procurement <procurement@cloudchain.com>
To: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-06-21T14:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor roster + SIG/CAIQ/SOC references

Priyom,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments — that's helpful. A couple follow-ups from procurement/security:
1) For KeyVaultOps, can you confirm whether they process any customer-derived telemetry that might contain identifiers?
2) Do you have a short signed attestation that no subprocessor has access to plaintext customer content unless explicitly provisioned by the customer? That is sufficient for our compliance team to advance for now.
3) We have a compliance template that requires signatures from both your security and legal; I'll send a link to the DocuSign powerform unless you prefer to attach a signed PDF.

Also, we'd like a KMS dataflow diagram that shows who controls keys, where they are stored, and any cross-border calls. Can Neha help with that?

Appreciate it — procurement is trying to close the loop by next week.

Regards,
Mark Ellis
CloudChain Procurement
procurement@cloudchain.com

Attachment: (none)

From: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
To: CloudChain Security <security@cloudchain.com>, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-06-22T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor roster + SIG/CAIQ/SOC references

Hi Aisha / Mark / team — forwarding a short technical note and a dataflow diagram (attached) to clarify KMS ownership and operational boundaries.

Summary (plain language):
- Customer-managed KMS: customers can bring their own keys (BYOK). In that mode, all encryption/decryption calls occur in a customer-controlled cloud account and keys never transit Redwood control plane.
- Redwood-managed KMS: keys are generated in a Redwood KMS tenant. Only the crypto gateway service has decrypt privileges, and the gateway runs in a hardened, isolated execution environment. Keys are stored with the cloud KMS provider in the same geographic region the customer selects.
- Third-party telemetry (KeyVaultOps, LogStream): permitted only to receive anonymized telemetry and service-level logs. We strip user identifiers prior to export. They do NOT receive any decrypted customer content or KMS material.

Attached: kms_dataflow_diagram.png (high-level, shows region boundaries and which accounts perform crypto ops).

If you'd like a short signed attestation, we can provide a one-paragraph statement on company letterhead signed by our Head of Security and General Counsel. Let me know which signers you require.

Neha Kapoor
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

--
Attachment: kms_dataflow_diagram.png

From: CloudChain Security <security@cloudchain.com>
To: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Cc: CloudChain Procurement <procurement@cloudchain.com>
Date: 2027-06-24T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor roster + SIG/CAIQ/SOC references

Neha / Priyom — thanks for the clarifications and the diagram. That addresses the outstanding technical questions. Two final asks before we mark the vendor assessment as "accepted":
1) A signed attestation (one-paragraph) that no subprocessor has access to plaintext customer content unless explicitly provisioned by the customer. Signed by Head of Security (Neha) and GC (Lauren) is preferred.
2) Confirmation that KeyVaultOps only receives anonymized telemetry and a short note on the mechanism used to sanitize identifiers.

If you can provide those two items by EOD Friday PT we'll be able to finish our review and proceed to procurement approval. If DocuSign is easiest, we will send the powerform link and include the compliance template.

Best,
Aisha Raman
Vendor Security, CloudChain
